results.question: How much is the monthly fee on the everyday account and how do I avoid paying it?
results.answer:
The Kaskazi Everyday Account costs **KES 250 a month**. Kaskazi Bank works out at the end of each calendar month whether the fee applies for that month. If either of the two waivers below applies, you pay nothing for that month. If neither applies, KES 250 is taken from the account at the end of the month.

You can avoid it in either of these ways:
- The KES 250 monthly fee is waived for any month in which your salary is paid into your Kaskazi Everyday Account.
- The KES 250 monthly fee on the Kaskazi Everyday Account is also waived for any month in which your average balance is KES 50,000 or more. Kaskazi Bank adds up the balance in your Kaskazi Everyday Account at the end of each day of the month, then divides by the number of days in the month.

You only need one waiver to apply. If you're self-employed or paid in cash, you won't qualify for the salary waiver, but you can still use the average balance waiver.

results.question: If I break my fixed deposit early do I lose my money?
results.answer:
No, you don't lose your money. If you break a Kaskazi Fixed Deposit early, you never lose any of the money you deposited, and your full deposit is always returned.

What you give up is part of the interest. You lose half of the interest earned so far. Kaskazi Bank pays you the other half, after withholding tax, together with the full amount you deposited. The money is paid into your Kaskazi account.

For example, on a KES 500,000 12-month deposit at 9.5% a year, breaking it after 151 days would mean you receive KES 508,351.54: your KES 500,000 plus KES 8,351.54 interest after tax.

You can't take out part of a Kaskazi Fixed Deposit. If you need only part of your money, you would have to break the whole deposit.

results.question: what does 'up to 50 days interest free' actually mean? do I get 50 days on everything I buy with the credit card?
results.answer:
Not quite. The 50 days is the most you can get, not a fixed amount for every purchase. Each statement covers about a month of purchases, and the payment due date comes some days after the statement date. A purchase made on the first day of a statement period waits the longest before it is due, so it gets the full 50 days. A purchase made on the last day of a statement period gets the fewest days.

For example, with a statement period of 1 to 31 May and a due date of 20 June, a purchase on 1 May gets 50 days, one on 15 May gets 36 days, and one on 31 May gets 20 days.

To keep the interest-free days, you must pay your full statement balance by the payment due date. The interest-free period does not apply to cash advances. If you pay less, interest of 2.5% a month is charged on the balance you carry over.

results.question: what happens if i miss one instalment on my personal loan
results.answer:
If you miss one instalment, a **KES 500 late payment fee** applies. It is charged once for that instalment, however long the instalment stays unpaid. Interest continues at your loan rate on what you owe. We do not charge a higher rate.

We try to collect the missed amount again when money next comes into your Kaskazi Everyday Account. Missed instalments are recorded on your loan and are reported to credit reference bureaus, which can make future borrowing harder.

If you know an instalment will be late, tell us before the instalment date. We cannot always waive the fee, but we can often agree a plan that avoids further missed payments. I can also check your loan details, such as your next due date and instalment, if you'd like.

results.question: My husband had a personal loan with you and he passed away last week. do we as the family have to keep paying it?
results.answer:
I'm very sorry about your husband. You don't have to keep paying the loan. Please tell us as soon as you can, at a branch or through this assistant, and send a copy of the death certificate. If a borrower dies, we ask a family member or the person handling the estate to tell us as soon as they can, at a branch or through the assistant, and to give us a copy of the death certificate.

From the day we are told, we stop collecting instalments and stop charging late payment fees on the loan. We make the credit life insurance claim; the family does not have to deal with the insurer. Any instalments collected after the date of death are refunded to the estate once the claim is paid. When the insurance pays, the loan is closed.

If any instalments were overdue before his death, we explain them to the person handling the estate and agree with them how they will be settled. We treat bereaved families with patience and do not pursue them personally for the loan.

A colleague will reply in this chat, usually within about 5 minutes between 7:00 am and 10:00 pm, and can take you through the next steps.

results.question: how is the personal loan interest worked out, is it linked to the base rate?
results.answer:

Interest is worked out each month on the balance you still owe. Interest is charged on the reducing balance. Each month we work out interest on what you still owe, not on the amount you first borrowed. The monthly rate is 15.5% divided by 12. Early in the loan, more of each instalment goes to interest; later, more goes to paying off the loan itself.

results.answer:
